quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When should you drive in a reversible lane marked with a red X?

options.text: When there is no oncoming traffic.
When you are passing another car.
Never.
Between sunset and sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: A red X means the lane is closed. Never drive in a lane marked with a red X. Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road. An oncoming vehicle is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming toward you, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Traffic fines in work zones are the same as normal traffic fines.
You must slow down for work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for equipment in work zones. Driving carefully in work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: You have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to cross before pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: When you have a green light, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection cross first. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop ahead.
Buggy warning.
Limited parking.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a stop sign is coming. Prepare to stop completely before you go through the intersection.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to speed up and match freeway traffic.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. Yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Cut quickly across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Change lanes safely, then put your vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: A traffic light is not working. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection looks clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop and look both ways before entering. Yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way over all traffic.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition affects how well you can stop your vehicle. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or in poor condition. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it hard to stop and stay in control.

questions.question: When you cannot see well, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down first when visibility is poor or road conditions are unsafe. This is your most important action.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what is true?

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less grip than paved roads. You must slow down. Your stopping distance is longer and you can skid more easily when turning.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, must you yield to drivers who arrived before you?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog when visibility is 500 feet or less. Do not use high beams—they reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is moving in both directions.

questions.question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
You have the right-of-way.
Force your way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will make room for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate, yield to drivers already on it. Merge safely when there is space.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, sound your horn if a child is about to run in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about braking and accelerating is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to ensure stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently and gradually so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: Should you use low beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop much faster than regular cars. If you follow too closely, you may not have time to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly. You need space to avoid a crash.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at an intersection, even without a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're trying to pass.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space when passing. Bicyclists have little protection, and passing too fast can push them off course.

questions.question: What is the speed limit for driving your vehicle?

options.text: The maximum speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for the current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must drive at a safe speed for current conditions. This includes following legal speed limits, considering traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light. Your speed must always be reasonable and prudent.
